Jeff had always been a bit of a loner. In school he was called weird and was bullied mercilessly by his peers. It wasn’t his entire fault though. At home he had to deal with a very abusive father who was always drunk and a junkie mother who wouldn’t hesitate in not feeding her son to get her fix. He loved his parents regardless, and although his father loved him in the wrong ways at time he felt no anguish towards either of them. You see, it was all of this that caused him to focus so much on school so he could get out of that place. In high school he finally got a scholarship to the college of his dreams; he graduated and left the small town that had tormented him his whole life. He had high hopes for his future and could not wait to make some friends for once and not be beat up, talked about, and hated. He had no idea of how cruel people could be though.

Jeff had a lazy eye, a limp, and he slurred his words really badly. Not to mention that he wasn’t in the best shape nor did he have a healthy relationship with hygiene. Everyone who saw him either pointed and laughed, had nothing but mean things to say, or tried to stay away from him completely. This didn’t bother Jeff at all though, for he was at the top of all his classes. The best grades, the best test scores, the best everything. The school called him a prodigy.

Out of school Jeff had found a job and started working, making his way up the corporate ladder. Everything seemed to be going fairly well, only he found himself lonely more often than not. When at work one day he looked up from his office to see the most beautiful girl he had ever seen, she was a temp who was filling in for the boss assistant after her sudden leave. He knew his odds he was 2 at tops and she was a solid 10, she probably had a line of guys waiting for her to even look there way. Jeff didn’t care; he knew he had to have her. Approaching the desk she was sitting at he began to get very nervous, she looked up when he reached and seemed to be taken aback a bit by his appearance. Jeff lost his nerve just like that and said he needed to schedule an appointment with his boss. She shot him a forced smile and said she would write it in his schedule. Jeff said thank you and walked back to his office cursing himself. He decided he would approach her again in the parking garage and ask her to dinner, even if she didn’t like him she might start to over a meal. Plus, who would turn down a free meal?

Ten minutes to closing he went down to the parking garage and waited. Then there she was, resembling an angel as she came out of the elevator. Jeff’s stomach fluttered and his heart skipped a beat. He approached her quickly and got her to agree to come with him to dinner. He helped her into his car and they left. She was extremely quiet as they drove and this was much to Jeff’s delight. He preferred the quiet ones anyways. He pulled his car up to his house and she looked surprised, Jeff turned to her, “Don’t worry dear, I will be cooking tonight, you can relax.” Jeff helped her inside and sat her down while he went to the kitchen to cook. Dinner came around finally and the meal was great. Similar to what you would find at a five star restaurant but Jeff’s guest barely touched her plate. He understood though, she was probably nervous too. They sat at the couch for a few hours watching movies and when it was getting late Jeff thought that everything had gone great. He hadn’t been this happy in a long time and he looked over to his companion, she had tears running down her face. He joined her in the crying because he knew she had felt the same. Moved to the point of tears. He was so happy and hadn’t felt anything like this in all his life. Jeff turned to her and said “I love you”, and with choked back words she looked deep into his eyes and said sobbing, “Please Jeff, untie me and let me go.”
Jeff had always been a bit of a loner.
